subject: Discovery recap — evaluation readiness & prompt ingestion plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Leila Morgan <leila@filterai.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@filterai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — evaluation readiness & prompt ingestion plan

Thanks again for the chat today — great to meet the FilterAI team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can move toward an eval pack and a scoped quote.

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary use case: conversational support and internal knowledge retrieval for customer support agents (mixed ticket + KB queries).
- Expected volume: ~1.2M monthly prompts, 75% short queries (<40 tokens), 25% long-context summarization (~500–2,000 tokens).
- Must-haves: PII redaction guidance, SOC2 evidence, and a tight latency SLO for live-support flows.

Recommended immediate items for evaluation readiness:
1) Prompt corpus: please share a representative 500–1,000 prompt sample that includes edge cases (attachments references, emails, partial legal quotes). We only need text rows; we will provide redaction heuristics.
2) Benchmark targets: we will run model candidates (LLaMA-2 13B-tilt, Redstone-Open-8Q, and a 70B quantized variant) against latency and quality metrics. I recommend we prioritize a 13B/8Q baseline for throughput, then 70B for quality checks on summarization.
3) Safety/redaction: attach our redaction checklist (redaction-checklist.pdf) — please confirm any internal terms that must be treated as sensitive.

Deliverables from Redwood (timeline):
- Eval plan + metrics spec (48 hours) — includes prompt binning, quality thresholds, and regression gates.
- Model suggestions and cost estimates for staging (72 hours) — short/long path recommendations.
- A shared Drive folder for prompt upload and a small intake form (link below).

Immediate ask from FilterAI: upload a 500-row CSV (prompt, context, expected_behavior) to the Drive folder and flag any rows with sample PII. If you prefer, drop raw exports and we will redact on ingestion.

Links:
- Intake folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-filterai-eval
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/FD-2027-0492

Next meeting: propose Wed Jul 7 10am PT to review first-run benchmarks. Let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0132

Attachments referenced: discovery-recording.mp4 (10min call recording), redaction-checklist.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@filterai.com>

Cc: Leila Morgan <leila@filterai.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — evaluation readiness & prompt ingestion plan

Thanks Hannah — that timeline looks good. Two quick clarifications before we upload:
1) The CSV we have includes some case notes with customer emails and order numbers. Can you confirm whether Redwood will handle initial redaction, or if we should strip those fields prior to upload?
2) For the summarization samples, a subset contains attached PDFs referenced by text (e.g., "see attached invoice"). We can’t share attachments in the CSV; should we include a placeholder token like [ATTACHMENT_REF]?

We’ll aim to get a 600-row sample into the Drive by Fri Jul 2.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Integrations | FilterAI
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@filterai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — evaluation readiness & prompt ingestion plan

Tom — quick answers and a little more color on model recommendations from the infra side: 
- Redaction: we can ingest raw CSVs into a private intake pipeline and apply our standard PII redaction layers (email, SSN, credit card patterns). If FilterAI prefers, we can do a pre-ingestion pass and return a redacted CSV for review before it hits storage. Either way, we keep the raw upload encrypted and access controlled.
- Attachment placeholders: yes, use [ATTACHMENT_REF] and an extra column attachment_hint (e.g., invoice, screenshot) — that helps with evaluating summarization behavior.

Model suggestions (first-pass):
- Throughput path (cost-conscious): Redstone-Open-8Q (13B quantized) — expected avg latency 70–90ms per token on our Dedicated config, good for high QPS.
- Quality path (long-form summarization): Redstone-70B-quant (8-bit) — higher latency but better compositional summaries.
- Safety/regression gate: run a lightweight classifier (our safety-scorer) on outputs and set a fail threshold for redaction-retention and hallucination metrics.

Benchmark plan: we’ll run three buckets — short queries, mid-level clarification, and long summarization — and report: Rouge/EM where applicable, factuality score (automated heuristics), and latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).

I’ll drop a short runbook and cost sketch to the Drive folder by EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clarity. We uploaded the CSV (filterai_prompt_samples.csv) to the Drive folder and flagged ~40 rows with obvious PII in the 'pii_flag' column. We used [ATTACHMENT_REF] placeholders and included an attachment_hint column as suggested.

Two requests before your team kicks off benchmark runs: 
- Can you confirm the exact spec for the CSV columns (we used prompt, context, expected_behavior, pii_flag, attachment_hint)? If you have a template, please share.
- For the privacy-first path: we may ask Redwood to run the first ingestion and return a redacted set for our review before you persist any data. What are the steps and estimated turnaround?

Also, any chance you can include a small sample run focusing on ticket escalation classification — we can surface a ground-truth file for 150 examples if that would help validate routing accuracy.

Thanks,
Leila
Leila Morgan
Product Lead | FilterAI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — evaluation readiness & prompt ingestion plan

Thanks Leila — I see the upload (confirmed). Quick responses and next actions: 

1) CSV spec: we prefer the following headers: id, prompt, context, expected_behavior (free text), pii_flag (yes/no), pii_fields (comma list), attachment_hint. I attached a one-page template to the Drive folder (see intake template).

2) Privacy-first ingestion flow:
- Step A: You upload to a short-lived intake bucket (pre-auth).
- Step B: Our intake pipeline applies deterministic redaction rules + regex patterns, produces a redacted CSV and a mapping manifest (kept encrypted, access-limited).
- Step C: FilterAI reviews the redacted CSV and either approves or requests additional redaction.
Turnaround: typically 24–48 hours for a 600-row file. We will not persist raw rows beyond the intake window unless you opt in.

3) Benchmark kickoff: we’ll start a baseline run using Redstone-Open-8Q and Redstone-70B-quant. Deliverables (by Tue Jul 6 EOD):
- Short report with p50/p95/p99 latency, cost estimate per 1M tokens, quality deltas on summarization buckets.
- Quality regression flags and recommended guardrails.

4) Classification sample: yes — please upload the 150-ground-truth file in the same folder and mark it as classification_ground_truth.csv. We’ll include a classification validation pass in the baseline run.

I'll lock Wed Jul 7 10am PT for the results review; calendar invite incoming.

Cheers,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments written to Drive: intake-template.csv, benchmark-runbook.md
